metadata.story_name: What's in the Water? (Algal Blooms & Fjord Productivity)

specification.unit_of_analysis: Fjord or coastal embayment (10–100 km scale); bloom patch (1–10 km)

specification_fit.variables: YES (multispectral; red-edge for pigments; blue-red for sediment/CDOM)

gotchas_avoided: Red-edge band (705 nm): excellent for chlorophyll discrimination
10 m resolution resolves fjord-scale features (1–10 km blooms)
Multispectral (11 bands) allows pigment decomposition (chlor vs CDOM vs sediment)
Can separate bloom from natural sediment plume
gotchas_hit: Cloud cover in high-latitude maritime: 5-day composite may blur rapid bloom dynamics
caveats: Frequent cloud cover requires composite strategy (5–10 day stacks)
Cannot identify harmful algal bloom SPECIES from spectrum alone; requires in-situ confirmation
Glacial sediment plume can dominate over low-biomass bloom signal
Red-edge band excellent but still indirect proxy for chlorophyll
candidates.validation_note: Explicitly in Stage 0 'Would Work'; red-edge band is key advantage over older sensors
candidates.next_step: Pair with in-situ sampling for species ID. Use spectral decomposition (IOP algorithms) to separate pigments.

specification_fit.variables: YES (OLCI designed for coastal color science)

gotchas_avoided: Purpose-built for coastal water color (OLCI = Ocean Land Colour Instrument)
Daily revisit catches rapid bloom onset/offset
Spectral bands optimized for chlorophyll, sediment, CDOM separation
Moderate resolution (300 m) ideal for fjord scale
gotchas_hit: Cloud cover still problematic for daily consistency
Slightly coarser than Sentinel-2 (300 m vs 10 m)
caveats: Cannot resolve individual bloom patches < 1 km (would need Sentinel-2 zoom)
Cannot identify HAB species from spectrum (in-situ required)
Glacial sediment can overwhelm bloom signal in sediment-rich fjords
Daily cadence great but must account for atmospheric correction uncertainty
candidates.validation_note: Explicitly in Stage 0 'Would Work'; designed for this science
candidates.next_step: Use daily composites for trend; pair with higher-res Sentinel-2 when cloud-free for detailed analysis

specification_fit.variables: PARTIAL (coastal band; green/red/NIR for vegetation index; lacks red-edge)

gotchas_avoided: 30 m resolution excellent for bloom patch detection
gotchas_hit: 8-day revisit gaps in active bloom season
caveats: Lacks red-edge band (705 nm): chlorophyll discrimination weaker than S-2
8-day revisit can miss bloom onset/decay dynamics
Lower spectral resolution for pigment decomposition
Coastal band not optimized for water color science (designed for aerosol correction)
candidates.validation_note: In Stage 0 'Would Work' but as secondary / backup, not primary
candidates.next_step: Use as archive for climatology (10-year trend); prefer Sentinel-2 or OLCI for tactical bloom detection

specification_fit.variables: PARTIAL (chlorophyll only; not sediment or CDOM)

gotchas_hit: ⚠️ RESOLUTION TRAP: User searches 'fjord algal bloom' → MODIS appears as daily global product
1 km pixel >> 1–10 km fjord features; coarseness destroys spatial detail
Cannot resolve bloom patches; only regional averaging
caveats: RESOLUTION FAILURE: 1000 m pixel >> fjord scale (10 km embayment = 10 pixels total)
Cannot detect individual blooms; measures regional average
Explicitly in Stage 0 'Wouldn't Work' for fjord-scale analysis
Only chlorophyll; lacks sediment and CDOM discrimination
Cloud cover gaps (daily nominal, not guaranteed every day)
candidates.validation_note: Exemplifies naive scale mistake: daily global coverage looks useful until you need fjord resolution
candidates.next_step: DO NOT USE for fjord bloom detection. Use Sentinel-2 or OLCI instead.

recommendation.approach: Paired multi-scale strategy: (1) Sentinel-3 OLCI (300 m, daily) for operational bloom monitoring (alerts, early detection). (2) Sentinel-2 (10 m, 5-day) for detailed bloom characterization when cloud-free. (3) Regional ocean models for primary productivity context. This stacks operational cadence with analytical detail.
refusals: MODIS: 1 km resolution inadequate for fjord features; useless for bloom-scale analysis
data_gaps: HAB species identification: no satellite observable; requires molecular/microscopy ground truth
Subsurface phytoplankton distribution: satellite sees surface only; models or float casts needed
Nutrient state (N, P, Si): not retrievable from color alone; needs biogeochemistry models or in-situ
recommendation.confidence: High (0.90). Top-ranked datasets align with Stage 0 predictions. Scale is adequate for fjord study.

stage_3_exploration_spec.test_region: Coastal fjord, high-latitude (e.g., Norwegian fjord or Alaska coastal region)
stage_3_exploration_spec.test_method: Bloom detection pipeline: (1) Daily OLCI chlorophyll anomaly detection. (2) Cloud-free Sentinel-2 spectral decomposition (OC3-like algorithm for Chl, IOP model for sediment/CDOM). (3) Validation against in-situ samples.
exploratory_queries: Does OLCI daily cadence catch bloom onset within 24 hours of peak?
Can spectral decomposition separate harmful vs. benign phytoplankton (proxy)?
How well does Sentinel-2 red-edge chlorophyll estimate match in-situ samples?
What is the glacier sediment plume signal vs. algal bloom; can we separate?
What is atmospheric correction uncertainty for fjord color in high-latitude conditions?
success_criteria: OLCI detects bloom initiation within 24 hours of in-situ Chl peak
Sentinel-2 retrieval RMS error < 20% vs. in-situ chlorophyll samples
Sediment/CDOM algorithm resolves glacier plume from bloom signal (R² > 0.8)
Spectral classification flags suspected HAB with > 80% agreement with species ID (when available)
expected_gotchas: Glacier sediment plume extremely bright; may saturate sensors or overwhelm bloom
Sediment plume and bloom can co-occur (glacial input drives productivity); hard to separate
Cloud cover frequency limits Sentinel-2 sampling despite 5-day nominal revisit
Atmospheric correction over sediment-rich coastal water introduces systematic bias
HAB species cannot be identified from spectrum alone; need microscopy
